items.stem: Which term matches this definition: “the layer above the troposphere, to about 50 km, where temperature rises with height because ozone absorbs ultraviolet radiation”?
items.answer: Stratosphere
items.markingKey: Stratosphere: the layer above the troposphere, to about 50 km, where temperature rises with height because ozone absorbs ultraviolet radiation. [1]

items.stem: Which term matches this definition: “the difference between the birth rate and the death rate, usually given as a percentage”?
items.answer: Natural increase
items.markingKey: Natural increase: the difference between the birth rate and the death rate, usually given as a percentage. [1]

items.stem: Give a reason for each answer. (a) A student writes: “Zoos are the best way to conserve endangered species.” Is this statement correct? Explain your answer. (b) Explain why the illegal wildlife trade threatens species such as rhinos and pangolins.
items.answer: (a) Not correct. Zoos can support captive breeding and education, but they hold small populations and cannot conserve whole ecosystems; in situ protection is usually more effective. (b) High prices for horn and scales (used in traditional medicine or as status items) encourage poaching; slow-breeding species cannot replace losses; poverty and weak enforcement make poaching attractive.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark correct judgement; 1 mark accurate explanation [2] (b) 1 mark per point up to [3]

items.stem: Part of an impact matrix for a wind farm gives each impact a magnitude (−5 to +5) and an importance (1 to 5). The score for each factor is magnitude × importance. water quality: magnitude −5, importance 4; air quality: magnitude −1, importance 4; traffic: magnitude −2, importance 5; noise: magnitude −3, importance 5. What is the score for water quality?
In a class discussion, a student says: “Reducing leaks in water pipes can save large amounts of water.” Is this statement correct? Explain your answer.
items.answer: Correct. Some cities lose 30-50% of treated water through leaks; repairing pipes increases supply without new sources.
items.markingKey: 1 mark correct judgement; 1 mark accurate explanation [2]

items.stem: Measurements on a 50 ha sloping farm show soil loss of 12 tonnes per hectare per year. Soil forms at about 0.5 tonnes per hectare per year. The soil has a bulk density of 1.3 t/m³ (1 ha = 10 000 m²). (a) Calculate the total soil lost from the farm each year. (b) Calculate how many times faster soil is lost than it forms.
items.answer: (a) 600 tonnes (b) 24.0

items.stem: In a class discussion, a student says: “An investigation should change only one independent variable at a time.” Is this statement correct? Explain your answer.
items.answer: Correct. Otherwise it is impossible to tell which variable caused any change.
items.markingKey: 1 mark correct judgement; 1 mark accurate explanation [2]

items.stem: With reference to the 2022 Pakistan floods, or another example of a flood or drought event, describe the causes of the event.
items.answer: Model answer (the 2022 Pakistan floods): Record monsoon rainfall (about three times the average in August), intensified by high temperatures, plus glacier melt in the north; the Indus overflowed and flat land in Sindh was submerged.
items.markingKey: Indicative content: physical and human causes, with data Level 3 (5-6 marks): well-developed points on both sides with examples and a supported conclusion. Level 2 (3-4 marks): some developed points, limited balance or example. Level 1 (1-2 marks): simple statements. [6]

items.stem: Table 3.3 shows annual carbon dioxide emissions (million tonnes) and population (millions) for selected countries (2022 estimates): China 11 400 Mt, 1412 million; Qatar 100 Mt, 2.7 million; USA 5 000 Mt, 333 million; Saudi Arabia 650 Mt, 36 million. (a) Identify the country with the highest emissions per person and suggest reasons. (b) Explain why total emissions and emissions per person give different pictures of responsibility. (c) Suggest why China has low emissions per person.
items.answer: (a) Qatar (37.0 t): high incomes and energy use, reliance on fossil fuels (coal or oil and gas), car use, energy-intensive industry or air conditioning. (b) Large-population countries such as China have high totals, but per person emissions may be low; small wealthy countries may have high per-person emissions but small totals. (c) Lower incomes and energy use per person, less industry and car ownership, and in some cases more renewable energy.
items.markingKey: (a) country [1]; reasons [1] [2] (b) [2] (c) [2]

items.stem: In one year the Philippines (population 60 million) had 526 000 immigrants and 290 000 emigrants. (a) Calculate the net migration rate per 1000 people. (b) Remittances sent home by migrants are worth 5% of the GDP of their country of origin. Explain why this is important for that country.
items.answer: (a) 3.9 per 1000 (b) Remittances provide income to families for food, schooling, health care and housing, support local businesses and bring foreign currency into the economy.

items.stem: Fig. 4.2 shows a simplified nitrogen cycle for a farm in Dubai, with fertiliser input, legumes, livestock manure, crops harvested and nitrate leaching into a stream. (a) Suggest how the farmer could reduce nitrate losses. (b) Explain the role of legumes in the nitrogen cycle on the farm.
items.answer: (a) Apply fertiliser in smaller amounts at times when crops are growing; avoid applying before heavy rain; plant cover crops in winter; grow legumes; leave buffer strips beside the stream. (b) Nitrogen-fixing bacteria in their root nodules convert N₂ into ammonium, adding nitrogen to the soil and reducing fertiliser needs.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark per method up to [3] (b) [2]

items.stem: A rapidly growing city has 600 000 people, each producing 1.1 kg of municipal solid waste per day. 45% is recycled, 5% is composted and the rest is landfilled. The landfill site has 5 million m³ of space left and compacted waste has a density of 0.8 t/m³. (a) Calculate the mass of waste sent to landfill each year. (b) Calculate the new lifetime if the recycling rate increases to 65%. (c) Suggest two ways the city could increase its recycling rate.
items.answer: (a) 120 450 t (b) 55.3 years (c) Separate kerbside collections; deposit-return schemes; landfill taxes; support and formalise waste pickers; education campaigns; recycling centres.

items.stem: Which term matches this definition: “when all people at all times have physical and economic access to sufficient, safe and nutritious food to meet their dietary needs”?
items.answer: Food security
items.markingKey: Food security: when all people at all times have physical and economic access to sufficient, safe and nutritious food to meet their dietary needs. [1]

items.stem: Which term matches this definition: “when there are too many people for the resources and technology available to maintain an adequate standard of living”?
items.answer: Overpopulation
items.markingKey: Overpopulation: when there are too many people for the resources and technology available to maintain an adequate standard of living. [1]

items.stem: State one difference between a destructive boundary and a constructive boundary.
items.answer: At a constructive boundary plates move apart and new crust forms; at a destructive boundary plates converge and crust is destroyed by subduction.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for a clear comparative difference [3]

items.stem: The volume of water stored in rivers is about 2 030 km³. The flow of water out of this store by discharge to the oceans is about 44 200 km³ per year. What is the residence time of water in rivers?
items.answer: 16.8 days
items.markingKey: residence time = store ÷ flow = 2 030 ÷ 44 200 = 0.0459 years = 16.8 days. [1]

items.stem: A news article states: “Burning fossil fuels moves carbon from a slow cycle to a fast cycle.” Is this statement correct? Explain your answer.
items.answer: Correct. Carbon stored for millions of years in coal, oil and gas is released into the atmosphere in decades.
items.markingKey: 1 mark correct judgement; 1 mark accurate explanation [4]

items.stem: Under the Paris Agreement Japan pledged to cut greenhouse gas emissions by 68% by 2030 compared with 2005. Emissions were 600 Mt CO₂e in 2005 and 414 Mt CO₂e in 2022. Calculate the average annual reduction needed from 2022 to 2030.
items.answer: 27.7 Mt CO₂e per year

items.stem: Explain how a temperature inversion makes air pollution worse.
items.answer: A layer of warm air above cooler air prevents air rising and mixing, so pollutants are trapped near the ground and concentrations build up.
items.markingKey: warm layer above cool [1]; no vertical mixing / trapping [1] [2]

items.stem: A researcher is investigating whether noise from traffic affects the number of bird species heard in urban parks in Santiago. The researcher used a different piece of equipment at the last two sites after the first one broke, and collected data on two different days. (a) Evaluate the reliability of the method. (b) Explain whether the conclusions would be valid. (c) Suggest how secondary data could support the findings.
items.answer: (a) Changing equipment may introduce a systematic difference between sites; conditions differed between the two days, so differences may not be caused by the independent variable; results are not directly comparable. (b) Conclusions are of limited validity because other variables (time of day, season, weather, duration of each count, the same observer) may not have been controlled and the sample may not be representative; a correlation would not prove that traffic noise level (dB) causes changes in number of bird species recorded in 10 minutes. (c) Compare with published studies, government monitoring data or long-term records for the same area to see if the pattern is consistent.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark per developed point up to [3] (b) [2] (c) [1]

items.stem: A palm oil plantation has replaced lowland rainforest in Borneo. It covers 5000 ha and uses fertilisers and pesticides. (a) Describe two environmental impacts of this farming system. (b) Explain how the farm could reduce its impact on nearby rivers. (c) Suggest why governments in some countries support the expansion of such farms.
items.answer: (a) Loss of habitat and biodiversity; greenhouse gas emissions; water pollution from fertilisers and manure; soil degradation. (b) Buffer strips of vegetation; precise fertiliser application; store manure safely; prevent animals from entering rivers. (c) Export earnings, jobs, rural development and tax revenue; food or fuel production for growing demand.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark each up to [2] (b) 1 mark per method up to [2] (c) [2]

items.stem: Table 5.1 shows birth and death rates (per 1000 per year) for selected countries. Germany: birth rate 9, death rate 13. Brazil: birth rate 12, death rate 6. Italy: birth rate 6, death rate 12. Pakistan: birth rate 26, death rate 6. (a) Calculate the rate of natural increase (%) for each country. (b) Suggest the environmental pressures that a population growing as fast as Pakistan may face.
items.answer: (a) Germany −0.4%; Brazil 0.6%; Italy −0.6%; Pakistan 2.0% (b) Increased demand for farmland, fuelwood and water; deforestation, soil erosion and water stress; growth of informal settlements with poor sanitation.
items.markingKey: (a) (birth rate − death rate) ÷ 10; two correct [1]; all correct [1] [2] (b) 1 mark per pressure up to [2]

items.stem: A company plans an open-pit copper mine in a forested valley near Bangkok. The ore grade is low and the processing plant will produce large volumes of tailings. (a) Describe two environmental impacts of the mine. (b) Describe how the site could be restored after mining ends.
items.answer: (a) Loss of forest habitat; dust and noise; water pollution from tailings or acid drainage; visual impact of pit and spoil; lower water table. (b) Reshape and stabilise spoil, replace topsoil, plant native species, create a lake or wetland in the pit, and monitor water quality.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark per impact up to [2] (b) 1 mark per point up to [3]

items.stem: Fig. 2.4 shows flood hydrographs for two drainage basins after the same storm. Basin X (urban) peaks at 85 cumecs 6 hours after peak rainfall; basin Y (forested) peaks at 30 cumecs 18 hours after peak rainfall. (a) Calculate the difference in lag time between the two basins. (b) Suggest why some people may oppose upstream tree planting. (c) Explain the purpose of land-use zoning on floodplains.
items.answer: (a) 12 hours (18 − 6) (b) It takes land from farmers, takes many years to reduce flood peaks and may not prevent extreme floods. (c) It restricts building in high-risk areas, so fewer people and property are exposed, and keeps the floodplain free to store water.
items.markingKey: (a) [1] (b) 1 mark per point up to [2] (c) [2]

items.stem: Which term matches this definition: “a resource that is naturally replenished and will not run out if managed properly, such as solar, wind and hydroelectric power”?
items.answer: Renewable resource
items.markingKey: Renewable resource: a resource that is naturally replenished and will not run out if managed properly, such as solar, wind and hydroelectric power. [1]

items.stem: Which term matches this definition: “pollution entering water from a single identifiable source, such as a sewage outfall or factory pipe”?
items.answer: Point source pollution
items.markingKey: Point source pollution: pollution entering water from a single identifiable source, such as a sewage outfall or factory pipe. [1]

items.stem: Explain the assumptions of the Lincoln index method.
items.answer: No births, deaths, immigration or emigration between samples; marks are not lost and do not affect survival; marked animals mix randomly; each animal has an equal chance of being caught.
items.markingKey: 1 mark per assumption up to [4]

items.stem: In South Korea, 12% of the population is aged 0-14, 72% is aged 15-64 and 16% is aged 65 and over. What is the dependency ratio?
A news article states: “Ecosystem services have economic value.” Is this statement correct? Explain your answer.
items.answer: Correct. Services such as pollination, flood control and water purification are estimated to be worth trillions of dollars per year.
items.markingKey: 1 mark correct judgement; 1 mark accurate explanation [3]

items.stem: Students sampled vegetation every 50 m along a transect across a sand dune system. Number of plant species: 0 m: 2, 50 m: 11, 100 m: 13, 150 m: 16, 200 m: 20, 250 m: 23, 300 m: 24. Soil organic matter (%): 0 m: 2.5, 50 m: 4.5, 100 m: 6, 150 m: 6.9, 200 m: 8.6, 250 m: 9.5, 300 m: 10.9. Explain the relationship between soil organic matter and the number of species.
items.answer: As pioneers die and decompose, organic matter increases; soil holds more water and nutrients, allowing more species, which add more organic matter.
items.markingKey: positive relationship [1]; explanation [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain why the height of the tropopause is greater at the equator than at the poles.
items.answer: Strong heating at the equator causes vigorous convection, which lifts air to greater heights (about 17 km) than over the cold poles (about 8 km).
items.markingKey: stronger heating / convection at equator [1]; greater height [1] [2]

items.stem: Fig. 1.5 shows land use around a large open-pit mine: the pit, spoil heaps, a tailings dam above a river, a processing plant and a new town for workers. (a) Describe two environmental impacts of the mine. (b) Suggest two ways the company could reduce the environmental impact during operation. (c) Suggest why local people may support the mine.
items.answer: (a) Loss of forest habitat; dust and noise; water pollution from tailings or acid drainage; visual impact of pit and spoil; lower water table. (b) Line and monitor the tailings dam; treat water before release; control dust with water sprays; store topsoil for later; replant spoil heaps progressively. (c) Jobs, higher incomes, new roads, schools and health care, and tax revenue for the government.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark per impact up to [2] (b) 1 mark per strategy up to [2] (c) 1 mark per point up to [2]

items.stem: Table 6.2 shows total renewable water resources (km³ per year) and population (millions): South Africa 51 km³, 60 million; United Kingdom 147 km³, 67 million; Ethiopia 122 km³, 123 million; Pakistan 247 km³, 236 million. Falkenmark indicator (m³ per person per year): 1700 or more no stress; 1000-1699 water stress; 500-999 water scarcity; below 500 absolute scarcity. 1 km³ = 10⁹ m³. (a) Classify each country using the Falkenmark indicator. (b) Suggest why a country with no water stress on this indicator may still have water shortages. (c) Suggest two strategies that a country with absolute scarcity could use.
items.answer: (a) South Africa: water scarcity; United Kingdom: no stress; Ethiopia: water scarcity; Pakistan: water stress (b) Water may be unevenly distributed in space and time (seasons, regions); lack of infrastructure or money (economic scarcity); pollution makes water unusable. (c) Desalination; recycling wastewater; importing virtual water as food; drip irrigation and reducing agricultural use; reducing leaks.
items.markingKey: (a) all correct [2], two correct [1] [2] (b) 1 mark per point up to [2] (c) 1 mark each [2]

items.stem: A hydrologist in Colombo is comparing two small drainage basins: one forested and one recently converted to housing and roads. (a) Suggest why the forested basin has a higher base flow in dry weather. (b) Explain the role of the Sun in driving the cycle.
items.answer: (a) More water infiltrates and recharges soil and groundwater, which slowly feed the river between storms. (b) Solar energy evaporates water and drives atmospheric circulation that moves vapour; gravity then returns water as precipitation and flow.
items.markingKey: (a) infiltration / recharge [1]; slow release to river [1] [2] (b) evaporation [1]; circulation / transport [1] [2]

items.stem: A class investigates whether the number of people using a beach affects the amount of litter found on beaches near Lima. The class chose sites where it was easy to reach, took single readings and did not record the weather. (a) Suggest improvements to the method and explain how each would improve the investigation. (b) Suggest how secondary data could support the findings.
items.answer: (a) Increase the number of sites (e.g. 10-15) across the full range of number of visitors; take three repeats and calculate means; random or systematic site selection to avoid bias; use the same calibrated equipment; collect all data under similar conditions. (b) Compare with published studies, government monitoring data or long-term records for the same area to see if the pattern is consistent.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark per improvement with explanation up to [4] (b) [1]

items.stem: Total fertility rate (TFR) in Bangladesh: 1975: 6.6, 2015: 2.1, 2022: 2. Replacement level is about 2.1. (a) Calculate the mean fall in TFR per year between 1975 and 2015. (b) Suggest reasons, other than government policy, for the fall in fertility. (c) Suggest the type of population policy Bangladesh is likely to need now. Explain your answer.
items.answer: (a) 0.113 per year (b) Female education and employment, urbanisation, lower infant mortality, higher costs of raising children and access to contraception. (c) Continued voluntary family planning while investing in education and jobs for the young population.
items.markingKey: (a) (6.6 − 2.1) ÷ 40 = 0.113 [1] (b) 1 mark per reason up to [2] (c) type [1]; reason [1] [2]

items.stem: Which term matches this definition: “the amount of dissolved oxygen used by microorganisms to break down organic matter in a water sample”?
items.answer: Biochemical oxygen demand (BOD)
items.markingKey: Biochemical oxygen demand (BOD): the amount of dissolved oxygen used by microorganisms to break down organic matter in a water sample. [1]

items.stem: Which term matches this definition: “the combination of different energy sources used by a country to meet its demand”?
items.answer: Energy mix
items.markingKey: Energy mix: the combination of different energy sources used by a country to meet its demand. [1]

items.stem: State one difference between open-pit mining and underground (deep) mining.
items.answer: Open-pit mining removes overburden to dig ore from a large pit, so it disturbs large areas of land and produces much waste rock but is cheaper and safer; underground mining reaches deep ores through shafts and tunnels with less surface disturbance but higher costs and risks to miners.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for a clear comparative difference [1]

items.stem: A researcher is investigating whether noise from traffic affects the number of bird species heard in urban parks in Karachi. Which is the most suitable hypothesis for this investigation?
options: There is more litter on beaches with more visitors.
Younger people recycle more frequently than older people.
Nitrate concentration is higher downstream of farmland than upstream.
Fewer bird species are recorded where traffic noise is higher.
items.answer: Fewer bird species are recorded where traffic noise is higher.
items.markingKey: It must match the variables in the investigation and be testable. [1]

items.stem: Explain your reasoning in each part. (a) A student writes: “Sustainable development means stopping all economic growth.” Is this statement correct? Explain your answer. (b) Explain why progress towards the SDGs varies between countries.
items.answer: (a) Not correct. It aims to meet present needs while protecting resources for the future, through more efficient and fairer growth rather than no growth. (b) Differences in wealth and investment, governance and corruption, conflict, debt, climate vulnerability and population growth; the COVID-19 pandemic reversed progress in many LICs.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark correct judgement; 1 mark accurate explanation [2] (b) 1 mark per reason up to [3]

items.stem: Atmospheric carbon dioxide concentrations measured at Mauna Loa, Hawaii (annual means, ppm): 1960: 317, 2000: 370, 2010: 390. The pre-industrial concentration was about 280 ppm. Assuming the 2000-2010 rate continues, estimate the year in which the concentration will reach 450 ppm.
items.answer: about 2040

items.stem: In a class discussion, a student says: “Biomes are distributed mainly according to climate.” Is this statement correct? Explain your answer.
items.answer: Correct. Temperature and precipitation determine the dominant vegetation, so biomes form broad latitudinal belts.
items.markingKey: 1 mark correct judgement; 1 mark accurate explanation [1]

items.stem: Mohammed argues that the demographic transition model is of limited use in understanding population change in low-income countries today. Discuss this view, referring to named examples.
items.answer: For: It is based on 19th-century Europe; today death rates in LICs fell faster because of imported medicine; migration, HIV/AIDS and policies (China’s one-child policy) are not included. Against: It still describes the broad sequence seen in Bangladesh, Brazil and Iran, where falling death rates were followed by falling birth rates; it helps predict future needs. Judgement: The model is a useful general framework but must be adapted to each country’s circumstances.
items.markingKey: Indicative content as in the model answer. Level 3 (6-8 marks): detailed, balanced discussion using named examples and data, with a reasoned judgement. Level 2 (3-5 marks): developed points but limited balance or exemplification. Level 1 (1-2 marks): simple, generalised points. [8]

items.stem: Fig. 2.2 shows sea surface temperatures across the tropical Pacific in December of a normal year and of an El Niño year, with arrows showing the trade winds. (a) Describe the normal pattern of sea surface temperature across the Pacific. (b) Explain how the trade winds produce this pattern. (c) Suggest how countries can prepare for El Niño events.
items.answer: (a) Warm water (about 28-30 °C) builds up in the west near Indonesia and Australia; cooler water (about 20-24 °C) in the east near Peru. (b) Easterly trade winds push warm surface water westwards; this allows cold water to upwell in the east. (c) Forecasting from ocean buoys and satellites; storing water and food; adjusting crops and fishing quotas; flood defences and emergency planning.
items.markingKey: (a) warm west [1]; cool east with data [1] [2] (b) [2] (c) 1 mark per point up to [2]

items.stem: A farmer in Kenya grows potatoes on 20 ha. Traditional methods gave a yield of 1.4 t/ha. After using improved seeds, irrigation and 100 kg/ha of fertiliser the yield rose to 4 t/ha. (a) Calculate the percentage increase in yield. (b) Calculate the extra production from the whole farm. (c) Calculate the extra grain produced per kg of fertiliser applied.
For a named example of an earthquake or tsunami that you have studied, describe the causes of the event.
items.answer: Model answer (the 2011 Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami, Japan): A magnitude 9.0-9.1 earthquake on the subduction zone where the Pacific plate is subducted beneath the plate carrying northern Japan; the sea bed rose several metres and displaced the sea, causing a tsunami up to about 40 m high.
items.markingKey: Indicative content: plate setting; magnitude; mechanism (sea-floor uplift, collision) Level 3 (5-6 marks): well-developed points on both sides with examples and a supported conclusion. Level 2 (3-4 marks): some developed points, limited balance or example. Level 1 (1-2 marks): simple statements. [6]

items.stem: Students counted organisms in a mangrove fringe: species A 12, species B 2, species C 5, species D 30, species E 30, species F 11. Simpson's index of diversity D = 1 − [Σn(n − 1) ÷ N(N − 1)]. (a) Calculate Simpson's index of diversity for the habitat. Show your working. (b) Explain why the index takes account of evenness.
items.answer: (a) 0.750 (b) The n(n − 1) terms give much more weight to abundant species, so a habitat dominated by one species has a low value even if many species are present.

items.stem: Which term matches this definition: “when renewable water supply is below about 1700 m³ per person per year”?
items.answer: Water stress
items.markingKey: Water stress: when renewable water supply is below about 1700 m³ per person per year. [1]

items.stem: Which term matches this definition: “the conversion of nitrogen in dead organic matter and waste into ammonium by decomposers”?
items.answer: Ammonification
items.markingKey: Ammonification: the conversion of nitrogen in dead organic matter and waste into ammonium by decomposers. [1]

items.stem: In a class discussion, a student says: “An EIA should consider social as well as environmental impacts.” Is this statement correct? Explain your answer.
items.answer: Correct. Impacts on communities, health, cultural heritage and livelihoods are usually included.
items.markingKey: 1 mark correct judgement; 1 mark accurate explanation [2]

items.stem: Annual maximum discharges were recorded for the Brahmaputra at Bahadurabad over 30 years and ranked (1 = largest). Recurrence interval RI = (n + 1) ÷ m, where n is the number of years and m the rank. rank 1: 881 cumecs; rank 3: 765 cumecs; rank 4: 678 cumecs; rank 8: 519 cumecs. What is the recurrence interval of the flood ranked 1?
items.answer: 31.0 years

items.stem: A news article states: “Earth Overshoot Day has moved earlier in the year since the 1970s.” Is this statement correct? Explain your answer.
items.answer: Correct. It moved from late December in 1971 to about the start of August in recent years, as demand has grown faster than biocapacity.
items.markingKey: 1 mark correct judgement; 1 mark accurate explanation [2]

items.stem: Table 3.3 shows annual carbon dioxide emissions (million tonnes) and population (millions) for selected countries (2022 estimates): Germany 670 Mt, 84 million; Bangladesh 100 Mt, 171 million; Nigeria 130 Mt, 218 million. Identify the country with the highest emissions per person and suggest reasons.
items.answer: Germany (7.98 t): high incomes and energy use, reliance on fossil fuels (coal or oil and gas), car use, energy-intensive industry or air conditioning.
items.markingKey: country [1]; reasons [1] [2]

items.stem: A student writes: “The magnitude of an earthquake is the only factor that determines how many people die.” Is this statement correct? Explain your answer.
items.answer: Not correct. Population density, building quality, time of day, depth of focus, preparation and secondary hazards (tsunami, landslides) are also important.
items.markingKey: 1 mark correct judgement; 1 mark accurate explanation [2]

items.stem: A group is investigating whether trampling on a footpath affects plant species diversity in a park near Accra. The group used a different piece of equipment at the last two sites after the first one broke, and collected data on two different days. (a) Evaluate the reliability of the method. (b) Explain whether the conclusions would be valid. (c) Suggest how secondary data could support the findings.
items.answer: (a) Changing equipment may introduce a systematic difference between sites; conditions differed between the two days, so differences may not be caused by the independent variable; results are not directly comparable. (b) Conclusions are of limited validity because other variables (quadrat size, time of year, soil type, slope) may not have been controlled and the sample may not be representative; a correlation would not prove that intensity of trampling (distance from the centre of the path) causes changes in number of plant species per quadrat. (c) Compare with published studies, government monitoring data or long-term records for the same area to see if the pattern is consistent.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark per developed point up to [3] (b) [2] (c) [1]

items.stem: A Sahel country has a population of 20 million and produces 3.9 million tonnes of grain a year. 30% is lost after harvest. Grain provides about 3500 kcal per kg and each person needs about 2100 kcal per day. (a) Calculate the grain energy available per person per day. (b) State whether grain production can meet the population’s energy needs and calculate the surplus or shortfall per person per day. (c) Suggest two ways of reducing post-harvest losses.
items.answer: (a) 1 309 kcal (b) No: shortfall of 791 kcal per person per day. (c) Improved storage (hermetic bags, silos) to keep out pests and moisture; better drying; better roads and transport to markets; cold chains.

items.stem: In a salt marsh, energy flow (kJ/m²/year) at each trophic level was measured: producers 36 000, primary consumers 3 590, secondary consumers 304. (a) Calculate the efficiency of energy transfer from primary to secondary consumers. (b) The gross primary productivity of the producers is 71 700 kJ/m²/year and the value given for producers is their net primary productivity. Calculate the energy used in respiration by the producers. (c) Suggest why a fourth trophic level is unlikely in this ecosystem.
items.answer: (a) 8.5% (b) 35 700 kJ/m²/year (c) Only 304 kJ/m²/year reaches secondary consumers; about 10% of this (30) would be too little to support a viable population of predators.

items.stem: Ethan argues that governments are more important than individuals in solving environmental problems. Discuss this view, referring to named examples. In your answer you should consider: NGOs; laws and taxes.
items.answer: For: Governments can pass laws, set taxes and subsidies, invest in infrastructure and negotiate international agreements (Montreal Protocol, Paris Agreement). Against: Individuals change consumption, vote, protest (e.g. Fridays for Future) and support NGOs; without public support policies fail; NGOs and businesses also play key roles. Judgement: Governments have the greatest power, but they respond to pressure from individuals and NGOs; all levels must act together.
items.markingKey: Indicative content as in the model answer. Level 3 (6-8 marks): detailed, balanced discussion using named examples and data, with a reasoned judgement. Level 2 (3-5 marks): developed points but limited balance or exemplification. Level 1 (1-2 marks): simple, generalised points. [8]

items.stem: Recharge of a coastal aquifer near Gaza is about 0.6 km³ per year, but abstraction for irrigation and towns is 1.8 km³ per year. About 20 km³ of usable water remains in storage. (a) Calculate the annual deficit. (b) Estimate how many years the usable water will last at the current rate. (c) Water-saving irrigation reduces abstraction by 40%. Calculate the new lifetime of the aquifer, or state whether it would become sustainable.
items.answer: (a) 1.2 km³ per year (b) 16.7 years (c) New abstraction 1.08 km³; deficit 0.480 km³; lifetime 41.7 years.
items.markingKey: (a) 1.8 − 0.6 = 1.2 [1] (b) 20 ÷ 1.2 [1] = 16.7 years [1] [2] (c) new abstraction 1.08 [1]; comparison / new lifetime [1] [2]

items.stem: Which term matches this definition: “a continuous, directed movement of sea water driven by winds, the Earth’s rotation and differences in density”?
items.answer: Ocean current

items.answer: Validity

items.stem: Give a reason for each answer. (a) A news article states: “Burning fossil fuels moves carbon from a slow cycle to a fast cycle.” Is this statement correct? Explain your answer. (b) Explain how human activities have altered the carbon cycle.
items.answer: (a) Correct. Carbon stored for millions of years in coal, oil and gas is released into the atmosphere in decades. (b) Burning fossil fuels transfers carbon from long-term stores to the atmosphere; deforestation reduces photosynthesis and releases carbon from biomass and soils; cement production releases CO₂; farming disturbs soil carbon.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark correct judgement; 1 mark accurate explanation [2] (b) 1 mark per developed point up to [3]

items.stem: Under the Paris Agreement Country X pledged to cut greenhouse gas emissions by 45% by 2030 compared with 1990. Emissions were 400 Mt CO₂e in 1990 and 340 Mt CO₂e in 2022. What is the 2030 target in Mt CO₂e?
State one difference between clay soil and sandy soil.
items.answer: Sandy soils have large particles and pores, drain quickly and are easy to work but nutrient-poor; clay soils have tiny particles, hold water and nutrients but are poorly aerated and easily waterlogged.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for a clear comparative difference [2]

items.stem: In a class discussion, a student says: “Most future world population growth will occur in sub-Saharan Africa.” Is this statement correct? Explain your answer.
items.answer: Correct. Africa’s population is projected to roughly double by 2050 because of high fertility and a young population.
items.markingKey: 1 mark correct judgement; 1 mark accurate explanation [2]

items.stem: For a named example of a city with severe air pollution that you have studied, evaluate the strategies used to reduce air pollution.
items.answer: Model answer (Beijing, China): The 2013 Air Pollution Action Plan: coal boilers replaced by gas and electric heating, factories moved, car purchases limited by lottery, electric buses; PM2.5 fell by about a third by 2017.
items.markingKey: Indicative content: named strategies with outcomes and limitations; judgement Level 3 (5-6 marks): well-developed points on both sides with examples and a supported conclusion. Level 2 (3-4 marks): some developed points, limited balance or example. Level 1 (1-2 marks): simple statements. [6]

items.stem: Students measured water quality on a stream in the Cameron Highlands at site A (500 m upstream of a paper mill), site B (50 m downstream) and site C (2 km downstream). Dissolved oxygen (mg/l): A 10.4, B 3.6, C 8.2. BOD (mg/l): A 2.5, B 10.9, C 5.3. (a) Calculate the percentage decrease in dissolved oxygen between site A and site B. (b) Explain the relationship between BOD and dissolved oxygen at site B. (c) Suggest how the students could make their measurements reliable.
items.answer: (a) 65.4% (b) Organic waste from the discharge is decomposed by aerobic bacteria; high BOD means the bacteria use up dissolved oxygen, so oxygen falls. (c) Take several readings at each site and calculate a mean; sample at the same time of day and depth; calibrate the oxygen meter.
items.markingKey: (a) (10.4 − 3.6) ÷ 10.4 × 100 [1] = 65.4% [1] [2] (b) organic matter decomposed [1]; bacteria use oxygen [1] [2] (c) 1 mark per point up to [2]

items.stem: A group is investigating whether trampling on a footpath affects plant species diversity in a park near Karachi. (a) Write a null hypothesis. (b) Identify the independent and dependent variables. (c) Suggest one ethical or safety consideration for this investigation.
items.answer: (a) There is no relationship between distance from the path and species diversity. (b) Independent: intensity of trampling (distance from the centre of the path). Dependent: number of plant species per quadrat. (c) Obtain permission from landowners or respondents; keep respondents anonymous; avoid damaging habitats; take care near roads or water; work in groups.
items.markingKey: (a) [1] (b) 1 mark each [2] (c) [1]

items.stem: Students in Kuala Lumpur studied succession on a sand dune system. Near the sea only marram grass and sea couch grew; 300 m inland there was heath and woodland with over 20 species. (a) Explain how the pioneer plants change the environment to allow other species to grow. (b) Suggest why soil pH falls with distance inland.
items.answer: (a) They stabilise sand, reduce wind speed, add organic matter as they die so soil forms and retains water and nutrients. (b) Shell fragments (calcium carbonate) are leached and humus from plants adds organic acids.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark per point up to [3] (b) [2]

items.stem: Part of an impact matrix for a shrimp farm gives each impact a magnitude (−5 to +5) and an importance (1 to 5). The score for each factor is magnitude × importance. noise: magnitude −4, importance 2; employment: magnitude +4, importance 2; air quality: magnitude −1, importance 5; landscape: magnitude −5, importance 3. (a) Calculate the score for each factor and the total score. (b) Identify the most significant negative impact. (c) Explain two limitations of using an impact matrix.
items.answer: (a) noise -8; employment 8; air quality -5; landscape -15; total -20 (b) Landscape (score -15) (c) Scores are subjective and may be biased; very different impacts are added as if equal; indirect and cumulative impacts are hard to score; it does not show who is affected.
items.markingKey: (a) scores [1]; total [1] [2] (b) [1] (c) 1 mark each [2]
